items.title: Canvas keys
items.summary: Adds the few single-key canvas shortcuts the original Tempo is missing. It never re-binds keys the app already owns, so nothing fires twice.

features.name: C opens the Comment tool
features.what: Before: the Comment tool could only be picked with the mouse in the bottom toolbar. Now: one key press toggles it, like clicking the button.
features.how: Press C while the canvas is on screen and focus is not in a text field.

media.caption: Pressing C, Shift+0 and ? on the canvas, with a key badge (fixture)

features.name: Shift+0 zooms to 100%
features.what: Before: zoom to 100% needed the zoom menu. Now: Shift+0 opens the menu and runs the app's own "Zoom to 100%" item.

media.caption: Shift+0 resets the canvas zoom to 100% (fixture)

features.name: ? shortcut sheet
features.what: Before: no quick list of canvas shortcuts. Now: a small card lists the native and the added shortcuts, with a link to the app's full shortcuts dialog.
features.how: Press ?. Close with Esc, ?, a click outside or the close button.

items.title: Canvas snap and Alt measurements
items.summary: Holding Alt/Option with a storyboard selected shows exact distances to other storyboards, like Figma. The app's own snapping is left as it is.

features.name: Alt shows the distance to another storyboard
features.what: Before: Alt measurements only worked for elements inside one storyboard. Now: hover a second storyboard while holding Alt and see the gaps between them in canvas px, as small red labels on thin red lines.
features.how: Select a storyboard, hold Alt/Option, hover another storyboard. Release Alt to hide.

features.name: Alt on empty canvas shows the nearest neighbours
features.what: Before: nothing. Now: with Alt held over empty canvas, the distance to the nearest storyboard in each of the four directions is shown.
features.how: Select a storyboard, hold Alt, move the mouse over empty canvas.

items.title: Browser frame on the canvas
items.summary: Places a live web page on the canvas next to the storyboards, with its own address bar. It pans and zooms with the canvas and is saved per canvas.

features.name: Add a Browser frame
features.what: Before: web pages lived only in the Browser tab. Now: a Browser tool in the bottom toolbar (or the + menu item "Browser on Canvas") adds a frame. An empty frame asks for a URL, then loads the page.
features.how: Click the globe tool or press W, then click for a 1280x840 frame or drag to draw one. Type an address and press Enter.

features.name: Move, resize and zoom like a storyboard
features.what: Before: not possible. Now: the frame moves, resizes and zooms with the canvas, with the same blue outline, handles and size label as storyboards.
features.how: Drag the header or the bar to move. Drag an edge or corner to resize (Shift keeps the ratio). Ctrl+wheel zooms the canvas. Arrows nudge, Delete removes with Undo.

items.title: Shader frame on the canvas
items.summary: Adds a live WebGL "Shader frame" to the canvas, with a side panel to edit it and export it. Idea and shader rules copied from pen.dev.

features.name: Add an animated Shader frame
features.what: Before: no shaders on the canvas. Now: a Shader tool adds a frame that renders a live GLSL shader. 8 presets are included. The frame moves, resizes and zooms with the canvas.
features.how: Click the sparkle tool or press S, then click (800x500) or drag to draw. Drag to move, edges to resize, double-click the title to rename.

features.name: Side panel controls
features.what: Before: none. Now: selecting a frame opens a panel with preset, speed, play/pause and one control per shader uniform (sliders, colours, toggles, textures). The frame updates live.
features.how: Click a shader frame, then drag a slider, type a colour hex or change the speed.

features.name: GLSL editor
features.what: Before: none. Now: a live editor shows the shader code with a compiler log. Errors are listed by line and the frame keeps showing the last working version.
features.how: Select a frame and click Edit GLSL (or double-click the frame body). Esc closes it.

features.name: Export PNG, WebM and embed code
features.what: Before: none. Now: the panel exports the current image as PNG, a 5 s WebM recording, or a standalone HTML embed snippet.
features.how: Select a frame and click PNG, WebM or Embed in the Export section.
